source_refs.note: Book p. 17: 1.6.2 text with Figures 1.10 and 1.11

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne logarithmic function ki saari properties alag alag saabit ki hain. Yeh topic un sab ko jor kar ek tasveer banata hai. Socho jaise kisi shakhs ka khaka (sketch) banana ho: pehle us ki khaas nishaniyan maloom karte hain, phir unhein jor kar chehra banta hai. Graph ke liye nishaniyan hamare paas tayyar hain.

Kitab kehti hai: logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) ka graph pichle subsections ki properties se banaya jata hai. Khaas taur par domain \(x > 0\), vertical asymptote \(x = 0\), intercept \((1, 0)\), continuity, injectivity aur \(a\) ki value ke mutabiq barhna ya ghatna (monotonic behaviour), yeh sab mil kar curve ki shakal aur jagah tay karte hain. In nishaniyon se base \(a\) ki mukhtalif values ke liye graph durust banaya ja sakta hai.
Figure 1.10 mein un logarithmic functions ke graphs hain jin ka base 1 se bara hai, aur Figure 1.11 mein un ke graphs jin ka base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai.

blocks.alt: Grid graph on a pale yellow panel, x from 0 to 22 and y from minus 8 to 12. Seven labelled curves y = log x to the bases 1.1 (purple), 1.2 (red), 1.3 (black), 1.4 (orange), 1.5 (blue), e (green, y = ln x) and 10 (dark blue). All rise from left to right, pass through the dot (1, 0) and drop steeply close to the y-axis; the base nearest to 1 rises fastest.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.10: logarithmic functions with bases greater than 1 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.alt: Grid graph on a pale yellow panel, x from 0 to 30 and y from minus 15 to 5. Five labelled curves y = log x to the bases 0.1 (green), 0.5 (blue), 0.7 (red), 0.8 (orange) and 0.9 (dark blue). All fall from left to right and pass through the dot (1, 0); the base 0.9, nearest to 1, falls fastest.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.11: logarithmic functions with bases between 0 and 1 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono figures ko parhne ka tareeqa, qadam ba qadam:
1. Har curve \((1, 0)\) se guzarta hai aur \(y\)-axis ke right side par rehta hai. \(y\)-axis vertical asymptote hai, yani curve us ke qareeb jata hai lekin usay chhoota nahi.
2. Figure 1.10 (\(a > 1\)): har curve upar ja raha hai. Dilchasp baat: \(x > 1\) par jis curve ka base 1 ke sab se qareeb hai, woh sab se ooncha hai. \(x = 22\) par \(\log_{1.3} x \approx 11.8\), jab ke \(\log_{10} x \approx 1.34\). Wajah: chhota base (jaise 1.3) ko 22 tak pahunchne ke liye bohat zyada power chahiye, to log ki value bari aati hai.
3. Figure 1.11 (\(0 < a < 1\)): har curve neeche ja raha hai. Yahan bhi 1 ke qareeb wala base (0.9) sab se tez chalta hai: \(x = 30\) par \(\log_{0.9} x \approx -32.3\) (figure ki had se bohat neeche), jab ke \(\log_{0.1} x \approx -1.48\).
4. Dono figures ek doosre ka aaina hain \(x\)-axis mein: \(\log_{1/a} x = -\log_a x\). Misaal: \(\log_{0.5} x = -\log_2 x\), is liye \(\log_{0.5}\) ka graph \(\log_2\) ke graph ko \(x\)-axis par ulta kar ke milta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Haath se \(y = \log_a x\) ka sketch banane ka hamara tareeqa (kitab ka sawal nahi, upar ki properties ka istemal):
1. Pehle asymptote \(x = 0\) (yani \(y\)-axis) ko dhyan mein rakhiye aur point \((1, 0)\) lagaiye.
2. Phir \((a, 1)\) aur \((\frac{1}{a}, -1)\) lagaiye, kyun ke \(\log_a a = 1\) aur \(\log_a \frac{1}{a} = -1\).
3. \(a > 1\) ho to in ko barhte hue curve se joriye, \(0 < a < 1\) ho to ghatte hue curve se; \(x = 0\) ke qareeb curve ko \(y\)-axis ki taraf mor dijiye.
Misaal: \(y = \log_2 x\) ke points \((\frac{1}{4}, -2)\), \((\frac{1}{2}, -1)\), \((1, 0)\), \((2, 1)\), \((4, 2)\), \((8, 3)\) hain. Tasdeeq: \(2^{3} = 8\), is liye \((8, 3)\) sahi hai.
Khud sochiye: \(y = \log_3 x\) ke liye kaun se teen asaan points lenge? (Jawab: \((\frac{1}{3}, -1)\), \((1, 0)\), \((3, 1)\).)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek aur baat jo figures se saaf nazar aati hai: log ka graph shuru mein tez barhta hai lekin phir bohat sust ho jata hai. Misaal: \(\log_{10} x\) ko 1 se 2 tak pahunchne ke liye \(x\) ko 10 se 100 tak jana parta hai, aur 3 tak pahunchne ke liye 1000 tak. Isi liye log ka graph lambi doori mein taqreeban seedha lagta hai, magar woh kisi horizontal line par rukta nahi; \(x\) jitna bhi bara ho, \(\log_a x\) aur bara hota rehta hai (\(a > 1\) ke liye). Exam mein graph banate waqt yeh susti dikhaiye, lekin curve ko flat line mat banaiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Graph sirf \(x > 0\) mein hai, \(y\)-axis ke qareeb jata hai aur \((1, 0)\) se guzarta hai.
2. \(a > 1\): barhta curve; \(0 < x < 1\) par \(x\)-axis se neeche, \(x > 1\) par upar.
3. \(0 < a < 1\): ghatta curve; \(0 < x < 1\) par \(x\)-axis se upar, \(x > 1\) par neeche.
4. Base 1 ke jitna qareeb, curve utna hi steep (tez dhalwan wala).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Curve ko \(y\)-axis ke paar ya \(x < 0\) tak le jana. Log function wahan exist nahi karta.
2. Curve ko kisi horizontal line par rukta hua banana: \(\log_a x\) ka koi horizontal asymptote nahi, woh dheere dheere magar hamesha barhta (ya ghatta) rehta hai.
3. Yeh samajhna ke bara base zyada steep curve deta hai; \(a > 1\) mein ulta hai: \(\log_{10}\) sab se sust hai.
